title: RNA Extraction From Human Tissue Specimens for RNA-Seq
author: Matthew R. Sapio
materials: Re-use collection tube in the next step.
Rest the tube for 00:05:00 at room temperature.
Make sure setting is at “g” not RPM.
In the meantime, label Qiagen spin columns and 1.5 mL sample tubes.

steps.title: Prepare RNase-Free Workspace
steps.instruction: Establish a sterile environment to prevent RNA degradation.

substeps.instruction: Set up an RNase-free area using heavy-duty aluminum foil and RNase Zap (or similar reagent), blotting excess with a clean Kimwipe.
Spray hands, bench, instruments (forceps, scissors, etc.), and tube holders with RNase Zap, then blot dry or rinse with RNase-free water.
Set up insulated buckets with dry ice and wet ice.
Set the centrifuge to 6 °C (to avoid accidental freezing; confirm temperature is ≥ 4 °C if excessive frost is observed).

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Tubes
steps.instruction: Organize all necessary materials and reagents before processing samples.

substeps.instruction: Ensure DNase stock is reconstituted and remove DNase buffer from the 4 °C refrigerator.
Prepare 70% ethanol by mixing 35 mL 100% ethanol with 15 mL ultrapure (RNase-free) water; label as '70% v/v, RNA-grade' with prep date and hazard sticker.
Arrange and label 2 mL homogenization tubes (gently sloping conical bottom for rotor-stator or bead beating tubes) and prepare two 1.5 mL conical centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Sample Recovery and Initial Lysis
steps.instruction: Retrieve samples from storage and initiate lysis while maintaining strict cold temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Remove samples from -80 °C storage.

If the sample is not already in the homogenization tube, chill the target tube and forceps tips on dry ice for ≥ 10 minutes, then transfer samples without defrosting (warm to -40 °C if samples are too brittle/springy to dislodge).
Add 200 µL QIAzol to sample tubes and return to dry ice to ensure a flash freeze until QIAzol fully envelops the sample.
Remove samples from dry ice and add 800 µL of room temperature QIAzol (total QIAzol volume: 1 mL) and proceed immediately to homogenization.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Mechanically disrupt the tissue using a rotor-stator.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize tissue by moving the rotor end up and down in the liquid QIAzol to ensure proper mixing.
Avoid extended homogenization to prevent whipping air bubbles, which can shear and emulsify phenol.
If processing multiple samples, wash the homogenizer with RNase ZAP and RNase-free water between samples, or swap for pre-cleaned rotor-stator attachments.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the aqueous RNA phase from proteins and lipids using chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Transfer samples to a fume hood and add 200 µL of chloroform per 1 mL of QIAzol (maintaining a 5:1 ratio).
Manually invert with shaking for 15 seconds and let sit for 3 minutes (do not vortex).
Centrifuge at 12,000 x g, 6 °C, for 15 minutes using a desktop centrifuge.
Return centrifuge to room temperature and leave open when finished.
Transport tubes back to the RNA bench without disturbing the layers.

steps.title: RNA Binding and Purification
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA using an RNeasy spin column.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette up to 400 µL of the clear top aqueous supernatant into new 1.5 mL tubes, avoiding the interface (suggested: 4x 100 µL with P100, then 1x 200 µL with P1000 followed by 2x 100 µL with P100).
Add an approximately equal volume of 70% ethanol to the sample tube and vortex for 5 seconds on low intensity.
Transfer up to 700 µL of the mixture to an RNeasy spin column in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 8,000 x g, 22 °C, for 15 seconds.
Add 700 µL Buffer RW1 to the spin column, let stand for 1 minute, centrifuge at 8,000 x g, 22 °C, for 15 seconds, and discard flow-through.

steps.title: On-Column DNase Digestion
steps.instruction: Remove contaminating genomic DNA from the bound RNA.

substeps.instruction: Perform on-column DNase digestion as specified (refer to the 'Perform on-column DNAse digestion' instruction).

steps.title: RNA Precipitation and Washing
steps.instruction: Concentrate and purify the RNA via ethanol precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Raise sample volume to at least 100 µL using RNase-free water.
Add 1/10 volume of 3M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) (e.g., 10 µL for 100 µL sample).
Add 2.5 volumes of ice-cold 100% ethanol (e.g., 250 µL for 100 µL sample) and mix by gentle inversion or pipetting.
Incubate at -20 °C overnight in a frost-free freezer.
Centrifuge at 17,500 x g, 4 °C, for 30 minutes to pellet RNA.
Carefully discard supernatant using a P-1000 pipette at an angle (hinge upwards), then remove remaining liquid with a smaller pipette.
Wash the pellet by adding 900 µL of ice-cold 70% ethanol; vortex briefly by hand or flick the tube.
Centrifuge at 17,500 x g, 4 °C, for 30 minutes and discard supernatant.

steps.title: RNA Elution and Recovery
steps.instruction: Dry and resuspend the purified RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Air-dry the pellet for 10 minutes (do not overdry; pellet should appear slightly translucent).
Dissolve the pellet in 50 µL RNase-free water.
If the pellet is hard to dissolve, incubate at 60 °C for 10 minutes.
Clean the Nanodrop stage: gently wet a Kimwipe with 70% ethanol, let evaporate, then repeat with ultrapure water and dry.
Blank the Nanodrop using the same aliquot/bottle of elution buffer (water) used for the samples.
Measure 2 µL of the sample; target 260/230 and 260/280 ratios ≥ 2 (samples < 1.8 may require sodium acetate precipitation).
Perform RNA quality assessment using the Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100; record RIN and electropherogram traces.
Note: Samples with RIN ≤ 4 are generally unsuitable for PolyA+ selection and should use rRNA depletion-based library prep.
